title: Netherlands – Repair and maintenance services of cooler groups – Onderhoud en levering van airconditioninginstallaties ten behoeve van het Landelijk Meetnet Luchtkwaliteit
description: Binnen de afdeling Meten Luchtkwaliteit (MLK) van het centrum Milieukwaliteit (MIL) van het RIVM is behoefte ontstaan aan de voortzetting van een onderhoudscontract voor airconditioninginstallaties ten behoeve van het landelijk luchtmeetnet, en de levering van nieuwe airconditioninginstallaties wanneer huidige airconditioningsinstallaties niet meer te repareren zijn. Het betreft de airconditioninginstallaties (binnen- en buitenunit) van ongeveer 52 meetcabines van het Landelijk Meetnet Luchtkwaliteit (LML). Tijdens de looptijd van de opdracht kan het aantal airconditioninginstallaties door Opdrachtgever met maximaal 15% gewijzigd worden in verband met aanpassingen in het aantal meetlocaties. De airconditioninginstallaties hebben jaarlijks preventief onderhoud nodig om goed te functioneren. Bij storingen moet de Opdrachtnemer binnen 2 werkdagen op locatie kunnen zijn om storingen van de airconditioninginstallaties direct op te lossen indien mogelijk om zo de continuïteit van de metingen te waarborgen. Ook zullen airconditioninginstallaties vervangen moeten worden wanneer die aan het einde van de technische levensduur zijn of niet meer te repareren zijn. Het doel van deze Europese aanbesteding is het sluiten van een Raamovereenkomst tussen het RIVM en één Opdrachtnemer voor onderhoud en levering van airconditioninginstallaties ten behoeve van het Landelijk Meetnet Luchtkwaliteit. De geschatte opdrachtwaarde voor deze aanbesteding bedraagt € 172.000,- exclusief btw op basis van de maximale looptijd van 4 jaar. De maximale waarde van de Raamovereenkomst over de gehele looptijd is € 227.000,- exclusief btw. Scope van de opdracht De opdracht betreft preventief en correctief onderhoud van de huidige airconditioninginstallaties, en de levering en installatie van nieuwe airconditioninginstallaties ten behoeve van het Landelijk Meetnet Luchtkwaliteit (LML). De opdracht betreft de volgende werkzaamheden: Preventief onderhoud bestaande uit het volgende: Één (1) keer per jaar een preventieve onderhoudsbeurt aan alle huidige airconditioninginstallaties (binnen- en buitenunits) van ongeveer 52 meetcabines verspreid over heel Nederland bij van het LML. Het aantal airconditioninginstallaties kan met maximaal 15% gedurende de looptijd wijzigen. Correctief onderhoud bestaande uit het volgende: Reparatie van de airconditioninginstallaties indien nodig, waarbij een monteur binnen 2 werkdagen op locatie dient te zijn en de reparatie direct uitvoert indien mogelijk. Onderdelen vervangen indien nodig na overleg met opdrachtgever. Levering en installatie van nieuwe airconditioninginstallaties en het afvoeren van de oude airconditioninginstallaties die hiermee vervangen worden: Het vervangen van airconditioninginstallaties die aan het einde van de technische levensduur zijn of niet meer te repareren zijn. Het afvoeren van oude airconditioninginstallaties die zijn vervangen bij de levering en installatie van de nieuwe airconditioninginstallaties. Looptijd Raamovereenkomst De Raamovereenkomst wordt gesloten voor een periode van twee (2) jaar. De Raamovereenkomst begint op 13 februari 2027 en eindigt van rechtswege op 12 februari 2029. Markkinakartoituksessa on kuultu alan toimijoita kirjallisesti ja markkinavuoropuhelun kautta, arvioitu hankinnan jakamista osiin sekä eri toteutusmalleja. Markkinakartoitus on toteutettu siten, ettei yksittäistä toimittajaa ole suosittu ja kartoituksessa on toimittu tasapuolisesti ja avoimesti. Markkinakartoitukseen ilmoittautui mukaan viisi toimijaa, joiden kaikkien kanssa järjestettiin Teams-tapaamiset sekä lähetettiin myöhemmin materiaalit kirjallisesti kommentoitaviksi. Kartoituksen keskeiset havainnot ovat, että markkinoilla toimii rajallinen määrä toimijoita, joiden tarjonta on pääpiirteittäin melko samanlaista. Etenkin kahviautomaatit sekä niihin saatavilla olevat tuotteet ovat hyvin samankaltaisia eri toimijoiden välillä. Palvelutasot ja niiden hinnoittelu vaihtelevat kuitenkin jonkin verran eri toimijoiden välillä. Lisäksi mahdollisuus tarjota kokonaispalvelua vaihtelee jonkin verran eri toimijoiden välillä ja pienimmillä toimijoilla ei ole välttämättä kapasiteettia tarjota kyseistä palvelua Espoon kokoiselle kaupungille. Tästä huolimatta Espoo tarvitsee palvelun kokonaispalveluna, koska kaupungin oman henkilöstön ei ole mahdollista huoltaa/ ylläpitää kahviautomaatteja sopimuskaudella. Hankinnassa päädyttiin siihen, että Espoo solmii yhden sopimuksen valitun toimittajan kanssa, joka voi halutessaan hyödyntää alihankkijoita sopimuksen toteuttamisessa. Kartoituksessa saatuja havaintoja on hyödynnetty hankinnan kohteen määrittelyssä, hankinnan rakenteessa sekä tarjousten vertailuperusteiden määrittelyssä. Markkinoilta saatiin tietoa ja lukuisia mielipiteitä liittyen hankinnan kohteen määrittelyyn sekä hankinnan rakenteeseen. Lisäksi vertailuperusteiden määrittelyssä saatiin kaikilta markkinavuoropuheluihin osallistuneilta toimijoilta mielipiteitä, joita hyödynnettiin vertailuperusteiden määrittelyssä. Hankinnan valmistelussa on huomioitu hankintalain 65 §:n mukaiset markkinakartoitusta koskevat periaatteet ja hankintayksikkö katsoo valmistelun tukevan kilpailun toteutumista. Hankinnan jakaminen osiin Hankintayksikkö on arvioinut hankinnan jakamista osiin. Hankintaa ei ole jaettu osiin, koska markkinakartoituksen perusteella kyse on kokonaisuudesta, jonka eri osat ovat vahvasti sidoksissa toisiinsa ja hankinnan jakaminen osiin kasvattaisi merkittävästi hallinnollista työtä sekä kustannuksia. Hankintayksikkö katsoo, että jakamatta jättäminen on hankinnan luonne, toteutustapa ja tarkoituksenmukainen toteutus huomioon ottaen perusteltua.

This Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) Sole Source Justification supports an FSS Task Order to be executed by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Enterprise Procurement Office (EPO), on behalf of the Veterans Transportation Program (VTP) within the Veterans Health Administration (VHA). Nature and/or description of the action, including a description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency s needs and the estimated value. VA proposes to award a non-competitive FSS task order to Duluth Travel Inc. (Duluth) to provide commercial air travel booking services for Beneficiary Travel. This program arranges air transportation for eligible Veterans who must travel outside their normal commuting area to receive authorized medical care. Supporting Beneficiary Travel, the contractor will provide: Reserving, booking, and ticketing of refundable airfare; Coordination of specialized airline accommodations (wheelchair assistance, etc.); VHA-compliant processing, documentation, communications and invoicing; Cancellations, exchanges, and itinerary management; 24/7 service support. VA will award this task order under Duluth Travel Inc.'s existing General Services Administration (GSA) Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) contract, number 47QMCB25D0001, issued under the Travel Agent Services category 561510. Duluth Travel Inc., a Small Business Administration (SBA) certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), is located at 2860 Peachtree Industrial Blvd., Ste 1000, Duluth, GA 30097-7906. Duluth is the sole SDVOSB under this MAS, there are no other SDVOSBs under this MAS. The value of this task order is $29,131,085.00 over a 12-month period of performance. This amount covers the cost of medically authorized Veteran airfare, refundable ticket fees, airline-imposed fees, and Duluth's per-transaction service fees for domestic and international bookings, discounted from Duluth's MAS contract. Authority: The statutory exception supporting the placement of this order on a sole source basis is RFO 8.401, specifically GSAR 538.7104-3(b)(1)(i): "The need is of such unusual urgency that following the procedures would result in unacceptable delays in fulfilling that need." Supporting Rationale: This contract action is necessary to prevent interruption in medically required Veteran travel services, maintain compliance with VHA Beneficiary Travel policy, and ensure Veterans can access authorized care when they cannot self-fund initial transportation. Beneficiary Travel booking support is a continuous, high-volume function: Veterans rely on it daily to reach specialty and other medical appointments that are frequently unavailable at their local facility. Any gap in this support does not simply delay administrative processing, it directly interrupts Veterans' ability to reach medically necessary care, including time-sensitive and recurring treatment. Many Veterans who require medically necessary travel cannot afford to purchase airline tickets up front and wait for reimbursement. This creates a significant barrier to accessing care, particularly for those needing life-saving transports. Without a contracted solution, Veterans may be unable to attend appointments, risking serious harm or adverse outcomes. The vendor is essential to ensure timely, reliable access to travel arrangements for these individuals. A full and open competitive acquisition for a requirement of this scope, scale, and specialized operational alignment would require sufficient time for solicitation development, a meaningful proposal preparation period, technical and price evaluation, and award and transition. That timeline extends well beyond the period VA can sustain without a booking mechanism in place. Compressing a competitive process to fit within a shorter window would itself create unacceptable risk of a flawed evaluation, increased protest exposure, and further delay, outcomes that would compound rather than resolve the urgency. Awarding to Duluth under its existing MAS contract avoids this gap entirely, because Duluth already maintains VA-specific workflows and operational infrastructure and can begin performance immediately upon award, without the stand-up period a new awardee would require. Absent this action, Veterans would be forced to self-arrange and self-fund travel to authorized care, or VA staff would need to revert to manual, non-automated processing, both of which increase the risk of missed or delayed medical appointments, disrupted continuity of care, and adverse outcomes for Veterans who depend on timely transportation to reach treatment not available locally. Contractor's Unique Qualifications: The VA's VTP office identified an urgent and compelling need to contract with a responsible source that can immediately mobilize and meet VA's specialized operational requirements for Beneficiary Travel. These requirements exceed standard commercial travel booking and include: compliance with VHA Beneficiary Travel policy and Federal Travel Regulation eligibility and reimbursement rules; coordination of medical accommodations (e.g., wheelchair assistance, oxygen needs) for a medically vulnerable traveler population; rapid, time-critical itinerary turnaround to prevent missed medical appointments; 24/7 booking and rebooking support; VHA-compliant documentation, invoicing, and reconciliation integrated with VA's internal systems; and nationwide scalability to serve Veterans across dispersed VA and community care sites. Market research confirmed that while 21 MAS 561510 holders offer general commercial travel services, only Duluth demonstrated existing infrastructure and experience aligned to these requirements, including established VA-specific workflows, proven nationwide scalability, and a track record supporting VA's travel programs. Duluth is uniquely qualified due to: VA-specific workflow experience; Ability to rapidly deploy nationwide medical travel support; SDVOSB socioeconomic alignment; Proven responsiveness and operational readiness; and Existing infrastructure already supporting VA travel programs. No other MAS vendor demonstrated the combination of VA-specific workflow experience, nationwide operational readiness, and SDVOSB status required to stand up compliant Beneficiary Travel support without impacting Veteran care. The impact on Veteran care is significant. While VA policy provides for medically necessary travel, the actual provision of these services is inconsistent across facilities. title: Ammonia-Assisted Regeneration for Longer-Lasting Direct Air Capture (DAC)
description: Every direct air capture (DAC) system depends on its sorbent, and every sorbent eventually wears out. This DAC from Los Alamos National Laboratory tackles that weakness head-on. It replaces the harsh release step with a gentler, ammonia-assisted process, which shields amine-based sorbents from the degradation that drives up operating costs. The method works with a broad family of established sorbent materials and support structures, so developers can build it into existing capture designs rather than starting over. Challenges Direct air capture is a two-step cycle: a sorbent captures CO2 from the air, then releases it as a concentrated stream. Liquid sorbents need expensive equipment and a lot of energy, more than 400 kJ of work per mole of CO2. Amine-based solid sorbents capture more CO2, regenerate at about 120�C and even perform better in humid air. Their weakness is durability. At release temperatures of 80�C and above, oxygen reacts with the amines to form free radicals and the amines can evaporate. Both effects wear the sorbent down over repeated cycles. Replacing sorbent drives up the overall cost of direct air capture and stands in the way of large-scale deployment. Problems Solved DAC changes how the sorbent gives up its captured carbon. First, the sorbent absorbs CO2 from ambient air at ordinary outdoor temperatures and pressures. Then, instead of relying on the conventional release step that damages the material, the method exposes the loaded sorbent to ammonia gas, which prompts it to release the CO2. Regeneration takes place at 75�120�C under reduced pressure (20�600 mbar), and the released CO2 can then be stored. The method is designed to prevent sorbent degradation and erosion. The application sets performance goals ranging from at least 50% of original capacity after five cycles to as much as 99% across 500 cycles. It applies to widely used amine sorbents, on supports that include silica, alumina, carbon materials and cellulose. Longer sorbent life means lower operating costs and a stronger economic case for direct air capture. Advantages Extends the useful life of capture sorbents and slows their breakdown Lowers operating costs by reducing how often sorbent must be replaced Works with many established amine sorbents and support materials Captures carbon at normal outdoor temperatures and pressures Delivers a high-purity CO2 stream for storage or reuse Improves the overall economics of carbon removal projects Market Applications Carbon removal and climate technology (direct air capture plants, carbon removal credit projects) Carbon storage and utilization (geologic storage, CO2-to-fuels and chemicals) Industrial gases (captured CO2 supply for food, beverage and manufacturing uses) Sorbent and specialty materials (advanced adsorbent production, sorbent coatings) Air handling and indoor environments (CO2 scrubbing in buildings, enclosed or controlled spaces) Energy and heavy industry (decarbonization strategies for utilities, oil and gas companies and manufacturers) TRL 2 S-167699 LA-UR-26-29519 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. title: Q-TAGG: Quantum Trapped-Atom Gravity Gradiometer
description: The Quantum Trapped-Atom Gravity Gradiometer (Q?TAGG), developed at Los Alamos National Laboratory, is a compact sensing platform designed to achieve extended atom interferometer interrogation times without the height required by conventional free?fall instruments. Ultracold atoms remain guided during interferometric evolution, providing a pathway to increased sensitivity within a compact architecture. The platform uses spatially multiplexed sensing, with multiple atomic sensing sites across one or more sensor heads operated under common or phase-referenced interrogation conditions. The resulting site-resolved phase measurements support estimation of spatially varying gravitational signals and differential processing of correlated disturbances. By combining a compact guided-atom architecture, spatial multiplexing, and suppression of correlated disturbances, Q?TAGG provides a pathway toward deployable quantum sensing for subsurface imaging, resource exploration, safeguards, and security applications. Overview Q?TAGG measures spatial variations in gravity using atom interferometric phase measurements acquired at distinct sensing locations. Optical pulses split, redirect, and recombine guided atomic wave packets. The resulting interferometric phase is sensitive to gravity and inertial acceleration along the relevant measurement axis, as well as to optical, trapping, and other instrument?related contributions. Multiple sensing locations are interrogated during a common measurement cycle, producing a synchronized spatial data set. After calibration and differential processing, relative phase measurements are used to estimate gravity field gradients and related spatial modes. The architecture also supports multiple spatially separated sensor heads for longer?baseline or distributed measurements. Technology Description Each sensor head prepares one or more ultracold atomic ensembles at respective locations within an optical guiding or trapping structure. The atomic ensembles are subjected to a common or phase?referenced interferometric pulse sequence and are read out on a site?resolved basis. Guiding the atoms during interrogation permits longer interaction times in a lower profile system than would be required for an equivalent free?fall distance. Because the sensing locations share common timing and an optical phase reference, their outputs are analyzed jointly. Differential and global estimation approaches are used to extract relative phase information, evaluate spatial consistency, and estimate gravity gradient signals. Common interrogation also suppresses disturbances correlated among the sensing locations. Multiple sensor heads can be arranged in linear, planar, or distributed configurations, providing flexibility in the selection of baselines and measurement geometries. Multi-axes sensing arrangements can also access additional components of the gravity gradient tensor. Advantages Guided atom interferometer operation supports extended interrogation without a tall free?fall structure. Spatial multiplexing provides multiple simultaneous phase samples within each measurement cycle. Joint processing of multi?site data supports gradient estimation, consistency checks, and systematic error diagnostics. Common or phase?referenced interrogation reduce sensitivity to correlated disturbances. Atom?based phase measurements support a repeatable, model?based calibration framework. Configurable sensor arrangements support different baselines and measurement geometries. Market Applications Geothermal and resource exploration (gravity gradient surveys of geological boundaries and density contrasts). Subsurface imaging and infrastructure (detection and characterization of tunnels, voids, buried structures, and changes around engineered sites). Environmental and storage monitoring (repeat surveys of groundwater, subsurface reservoirs, carbon storage sites, and changing mass distributions). Security and nuclear safeguards (passive detection or monitoring of gravity anomalies associated with dense objects). Mobile surveying and navigation (moving platform gravity mapping and gravity-referenced positioning following dynamic validation). Space-based Earth observation (gravity mapping for geodesy, hydrology and climate monitoring).
